name: Sonnet global diversification via US-listed ADRs and ETFs
strategy: Rotate the core toward international/EM ETFs and quality non-US ADRs that lagged the US AI-infra rally, keep crypto exposure at zero given the deep bear trend, and hold a modest inverse-ETF hedge plus elevated cash against US mega-cap AI-valuation risk.

positions.thesis: Broad EM ETF core exposure; kept below single-country legs in size since the fund is ~46% tech-weighted (TSM/Samsung top holdings) and thus a less clean diversifier from the US-AI trade than it's labeled as. No news shift this week.

Best-in-class semis ADR; still Strong Buy with average PT ~$547 (+28% upside from $426), ramping 3nm production for AI demand, exploring a Sony image-sensor JV. Modest "too expensive" chatter but no downgrade -- unchanged.

Monopoly lithography maker, +73% YTD; consensus PT $2176 (+18% from $1844) and 17% interim dividend hike reaffirm the franchise. Some valuation-fatigue commentary emerging but no Strong-Buy erosion -- unchanged.
Brazil ETF, low correlation to the US AI-valuation trade; top holding Nu Holdings just jumped 10% to a 5-month high, supportive of the ETF. Unchanged conviction.
Japan ETF, governance-reform tailwind independent of the US AI drawdown/rally cycle. No adverse news this week -- unchanged.

China ADR, still resilient (Apple tapping Alibaba for a China-specific AI model, 3B+ AI model downloads, some analysts see it 37% undervalued) but earnings land 8/20, after this book's next scheduled review -- adding a -12% stop now closes that unprotected downside gap through a binary print plus the standing shareholder-litigation overhang, at no cost unless triggered.
India ETF, structural EM growth diversification with low correlation to the US AI trade; unchanged.

Modest inverse-Nasdaq hedge against US mega-cap AI-valuation risk. Down ~3% over the past week as QQQ held near its highs (Burry reportedly shorting QQQ/Micron on valuation, but no confirmed correction yet) -- exactly the expected drag from a hedge in a grinding-up tape; far from stop/TP, size stays modest per mandate.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Weekly check across all 8 positions found no thesis-breaking news since the 8/10 entry (TSM $426, ASML $1844, EWZ, EWJ, EEM, INDA, SQQQ all tracking prior theses with no new catalysts) so the book is otherwise left untouched -- one addition: BABA reports earnings 8/20, which falls after this book's next scheduled weekly review (8/22), leaving the position unprotected on the downside through a binary catalyst for over a week. Adding a stop-loss closes that gap at zero cost unless triggered; TP+25% (already trimmed last week for this same event) and all other 7 legs, sizes and cash are unchanged.
